content.text: {"overall_verdict":"MEETS_WITH_LIMITED_GAPS","verdict_reason":"The chapter's integrated core survives under the frozen premises: it retains the received readings ('the received reading is true,' 'the north reading remains true'), derives each alternate hearing from the same consonants with attested or productively derived lexemes, stages words before symbols, and consumes a background symbol system that was frozen independently in the prior chapter. However, a small number of outcome-relevant gaps remain: the chapter asserts intended double hearings ('spoken once, heard twice,' 'the words have earned their readings') where the rubric licenses only admissibility; the Hithpael 'silence' hearing and the suffixed keseh hearing rest on productive-but-unattested combinations that should carry an explicit underdetermination label; the calendar-phase paragraph leans on a full-moon month-head background hypothesis that the packet asserts but does not independently establish; and the chapter never performs Rule 4's explicit comparison against the strongest complete rival joint model or states reversal conditions.","rule_audit":[{"rule":"1","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"The Masoretic pointing is treated as one reading tradition without a head start, and the chapter repeatedly retains the pointed reading as true alongside its alternates. But where the comparison between the pointed reading and the added hearing is underdetermined (eddammeh, kis'i), the chapter asserts both as jointly intended and disclosed rather than labeling the second hearing 'admissible; comparison underdetermined.'"},{"rule":"2","result":"PASS","reason":"Strong's, Gesenius, and the ASV are cited for data and arguments (spellings, attested senses, grammatical mechanisms), not as status-based proof. No appeal to tradition, majority, or authority is used to decide a reading. One minor lean: Strong's etymology of kisse' as a 'covered seat' is reported as fact rather than as one lexicographic proposal, but no conclusion turns solely on it."},{"rule":"3","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"Most alternates pass the symmetrical gate cleanly on the same consonants: shachar 'be black' is attested (Job 30:30) and expressly labeled wordplay; tsafun 'hidden' is attested (Ps 83:3; Ezek 7:22); keseh is attested with both spellings (Prov 7:20; Ps 81:3). The received readings pass equally. Two items are marginal: keseh with a 1cs pronominal suffix is unattested (productive morphology only), and the Hithpael of the 'silence' root is admittedly unattested anywhere, resting on a productive stem function plus le-marked objects. Gate item 4 permits productive rules, so these are admissible, but the chapter's own footnote is the only place the thinness is disclosed, and admissibility is elsewhere allowed to read as demonstration."},{"rule":"4","result":"PARTIAL","reason":"Stages 1-3 are respected: the celestial symbol system was frozen in the prior chapter without the target passage, each candidate reading is derived before the symbols enter, and the background's predictions (moon marks moedim; throne-keseh link) are stated. Stages 4-7 are incomplete: the chapter never audits the strongest rival joint model (received hubris reading plus the packet's own stars-as-host court symbolism, which explains har moed, tsaphon via Ps 48, and the cloud without eclipse machinery), reuses Ps 89:36-37 in both background and target without an explicit dependency note, and states no reversal evidence."}],"claim_ledger":[{"claim":"Helel ben shachar can be heard both as 'son of the dawn' and, by same-consonant wordplay, as 'son/bearer of blackness' (verb shachar, Job 30:30), characterizing one who appears bright but produces darkness.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"ben shachar with the 'be black' root heard as a characterizing wordplay alongside the dawn noun","strongest_rival":"Masoretic 'son of the dawn' (noun shachar) as the sole sense","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"NOT_COMPARATIVE","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The verb 'be black' is independently attested (Job 30:30), the consonants are identical, and the chapter's own footnote explicitly disclaims a grammatical-victory claim, presenting a characterization wordplay while keeping the dawn reading. Evaluator knowledge confirms H7835/H7837 are distinct lexemes on the same consonants (requires source verification).","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Evidence that 'ben + quality-noun' characterization is not a productive Hebrew idiom, or that the blackness root cannot yield a nominal sense in this construction."},{"claim":"Har moed means the mountain of the appointed assembly, with moed's full lexical field (appointed time, place, meeting; Lev 23:2) legitimately in view.","category":"LEXICAL_OR_GRAMMATICAL","book_candidate":"moed carrying its appointed-times field, linking the mountain to the covenant assembly and calendar","strongest_rival":"moed as 'assembly/council' only (the gathered divine or royal court), with no calendar overtone","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The lexical field claim is sound: moed demonstrably spans appointed time, meeting, and place (Lev 23:2; ohel moed). Whether Isaiah intends the calendar overtone in this unique construct phrase cannot be selected from the packet; both senses cohere in the clause.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A demonstration that har moed is a fixed idiom attested elsewhere with a single frozen sense, excluding the appointed-times overtone."},{"claim":"Yarkete tsaphon can be heard both as 'recesses of the north' (retained as true, per Ps 48:2 of Zion) and as 'innermost recesses of the hidden place' (tsafun; Ezek 7:22; Ps 83:3).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"tsafun 'hidden/treasured' as a second hearing on the same consonants, with north retained","strongest_rival":"Masoretic tsaphon 'north' alone (with Ps 48:2's Zion association)","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"Both hearings use the identical consonants; tsafun as qal passive participle is independently attested in the cited senses. The chapter does not displace 'north' and cites Ps 48:2 for it, so both pass; whether the second hearing is authorially intended is not decidable from the packet.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Evidence that yarkete tsaphon is a fixed geographic formula whose second element never admits the participial reading in construct with yarkete."},{"claim":"Isaiah's 'my throne' (kis'i) can also be heard as 'my full moon,' because kisse' and keseh share both spellings (Prov 7:20 spells full moon as kaph-samekh-aleph; Ps 81:3 as kaph-samekh-he; Job 26:9 writes the throne with the second spelling under a covering cloud), and Ps 89:36-37 binds throne to sun and moon.","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"kis'i heard secondarily as the suffixed full-moon word, a 'covered lunar seat'","strongest_rival":"kis'i as 'my throne' only, the plain and universal sense of the suffixed noun","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The spelling facts are verifiable and correct (evaluator knowledge confirms Prov 7:20 kese' with aleph, Ps 81:3 keseh with he, and Job 26:9's disputed kisseh/keseh; requires source verification). However, keseh is never attested with a pronominal suffix, so the book's hearing passes only on productive morphology, while 'my throne' is massively attested. The chapter frames it as a second hearing, not a replacement, which the gate permits; as a comparative claim the rival is better supported as the primary sense.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"An attested suffixed form of keseh anywhere in Hebrew literature would strengthen the hearing; a morphological demonstration that keseh cannot take a suffix in the kis'i form would eliminate it."},{"claim":"The consonants aleph-dalet-mem-he before le-elyon can be heard both as 'I will make myself like the Most High' (damah I) and as 'I will bring the Highest to silence for myself' (damah III, Hithpael for-oneself with le-marked object; Isa 15:1; Hos 4:5).","category":"LINGUISTIC_VOCALIZATION","book_candidate":"Hithpael of the silence-root with external le-object as a second hearing","strongest_rival":"Masoretic eddammeh from damah I 'resemble,' the standard idiom with le","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"RIVAL_BETTER_SUPPORTED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The rival is the plainly attested construction (damah + le 'be like,' cf. Ezek 31). The book's hearing uses only productive machinery: the transitive silence sense is attested in other stems (Hos 4:5 qal; Isa 15:1 niphal), the Hithpael for-oneself function and le-marked objects are real Hebrew phenomena (Gesenius citations require source verification), but no Hithpael of this root exists anywhere, which the chapter's footnote candidly admits. Gate item 4 admits it as a productive formation, so it passes admission; comparatively the rival is better supported, and the chapter itself concedes 'neither reading needs to defeat the other.' The residual claim that Isaiah intends both is underdetermined.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_OVERCLAIM","outcome_changing_evidence":"Any attested Hithpael of a destruction/cessation root taking a le-marked external object would substantially raise the hearing's weight; a demonstration that assimilated-taw Hithpael of dalet-initial roots cannot yield this consonantal form would eliminate it."},{"claim":"The symbols apply as previously derived: stars = the righteous (Dan 12:3), mountain = kingdom (Dan 2:35,44), the moon governs the moedim (Gen 1:14; Ps 104:19; Lev 23:2), and the sun is the sign of the Most High (Gen 1:16; Ps 84:11).","category":"SYMBOLIC_DERIVATION","book_candidate":"stars of God = the covenant righteous whom the rebel seeks to rise above","strongest_rival":"stars of God = the heavenly host/court (1 Kgs 22:19; Job 38:7), i.e., angelic beings, a reading the background packet itself also supports","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["BACKGROUND_PACKET","TARGET_CHAPTER"],"reason":"Each identification is derived from Old Testament texts per premise 5 and was established in the frozen background chapter, which however supports both the righteous-stars and host-stars readings (it explicitly merges them: the elders stand among the host). Either referent leaves the chapter's structure intact, so the packet does not select between them and does not need to.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"A contextual demonstration that 'stars of God' in Isa 14:13 is a fixed idiom for one referent class exclusively."},{"claim":"Read spatially, the boast describes raising a darkness-covered lunar seat into the sun's apparent place — becoming 'like' the Highest by substitution and 'silencing' the Highest Light by covering it (Ps 19:1-6; Isa 5:20; 2 Cor 11:14).","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","book_candidate":"the eclipse-figure synthesis as the unifying disclosure of the five declarations","strongest_rival":"the received hubris reading alone: a taunt over the king of Babylon's ambition to join/exceed the divine court on the mount of assembly, with no celestial-mechanics overlay","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","BACKGROUND_PACKET","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"As a synthesis it is coherent, retains the received reading, and unifies several otherwise independent details (moed, the covered seat, the dark cloud, the spatial verbs, Dan 7:25, Amos 8:9-10). But its comparative superiority over the plain reading is never tested against the rival joint model as Rule 4 stage 4 requires, and much of the fit is accommodation after the fact, which Rule 4 assigns little weight. Admissible as a complementary layer; not demonstrated as the disclosed meaning.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"An explicit rival joint-model audit showing the eclipse synthesis explains facts the hubris reading leaves unexplained at lower assumption cost, or predicts a textual detail not used to build it."},{"claim":"Astronomical facts: a full moon stands opposite the sun and can never eclipse it; only the moon at dark conjunction can enter the sun's apparent position; Passover falls at full moon; natural totality lasts minutes, not three hours.","category":"HISTORICAL_OR_ASTRONOMICAL","book_candidate":"the stated eclipse mechanics and Passover-phase facts","strongest_rival":"none — these are uncontested physical/calendrical facts","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"NOT_APPLICABLE","comparison":"NOT_COMPARATIVE","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"All stated astronomy is correct by evaluator knowledge (requires source verification only in the trivial sense). The chapter correctly refuses to call the crucifixion darkness a natural eclipse rather than smuggling an impossible one in.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"None; these facts are not in dispute."},{"claim":"Amos 8:9-10 (sun down at noon, feast turned to mourning, grief of an only son) is prophetically joined to the crucifixion darkness (Matt 27:45; Luke 23:44-45 'the sun's light failing'), NT confirmation of an OT-derived pattern per premise 8.","category":"THEOLOGICAL_SYNTHESIS","book_candidate":"Amos 8 as the prior-scripture frame that the Gospel darkness fulfills","strongest_rival":"Amos 8:9-10 as judgment imagery on eighth-century Israel with no forward referent","book_admission":"PASS","rival_admission":"PASS","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["TARGET_CHAPTER","EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE"],"reason":"The synthesis follows the required direction (Prophets first, NT as confirmation) and the convergence of three named details (noon darkness, feast, only son) is a genuine unification rather than a single-point fit. Luke's 'sun's light failing' (tou heliou eklipontos) is the critical-text reading behind the ASV — evaluator knowledge, requires source verification, and the chapter should note it is one textual stream. Selection between typological and exhausted-historical readings is a canonical-premise question the packet's premises permit but do not force.","gap_owner":"NONE","outcome_changing_evidence":"Evidence that Luke's eklipontos reading is secondary in the earliest recoverable text would weaken one supporting detail without collapsing the Matthew/Amos convergence."},{"claim":"Daniel 7:25 names the plan's historical work (wearing out the saints, thinking to change times and laws), and the phase matters: a month begun at the hidden conjunction rather than the full moon inverts the lights, the counterfeit ruling from the phase that can cover the sun.","category":"BACKGROUND_HYPOTHESIS","book_candidate":"the full-moon month-head calendar, against which conjunction-reckoning is the inversion","strongest_rival":"conjunction or first-crescent month-head reckoning as the original biblical practice","book_admission":"UNDERDETERMINED","rival_admission":"UNDERDETERMINED","comparison":"UNDERDETERMINED","evidence_origins":["BACKGROUND_PACKET","TARGET_CHAPTER"],"reason":"The Dan 7:25 linkage (times and saints attacked in one sentence) is a fair synthesis. But the full-moon month-head hypothesis is asserted in the background packet ('the full moon standing at her feet marks the head of the year') without the independent derivation being present in this packet; Ps 81:3 (keseh on our feast day) is suggestive but not decisive here. Neither calendar candidate is established by the supplied evidence, and the chapter's inversion argument presupposes the book's side.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","outcome_changing_evidence":"The independent Torah/Prophets derivation of the month-head phase (apparently housed elsewhere in the book) supplied or cross-cited; or a Torah-based demonstration of conjunction/crescent reckoning, which would reverse the inversion claim."}],"reciprocal_consilience":{"verdict":"VALID_BUT_INCOMPLETE","independent_background_support":"The celestial-household symbol system was established in the frozen prior chapter from Gen 1:14-18, Gen 37:9-10 (Jacob's own interpretation), Ps 84:11, Ps 89:36-37, Ps 136:8-9, Dan 12:3, and Job 38:32 — none of it drawn from Isaiah 14. That background genuinely predates the target in logical order and predicts that a usurpation of the lights would target the moon (the sign of the appointed times) and the sun's apparent office.","incremental_target_evidence":"The target contributes evidence not used to build the background: Isaiah 14's specific vocabulary cluster (moed, yarkete tsaphon/tsafun, av/bamah, the spatial verb chain), the keseh spelling data (Prov 7:20; Ps 81:3; Job 26:9), the eddammeh double-root observation, Amos 8:9-10, and Dan 7:25. These are nonduplicative and give the joint model real unification work.","dependency_or_duplication_risk":"Ps 89:36-37 is used in the background to seat the moon as throne/faithful witness and again in the target to bind Isaiah's throne to lunar fulness; it must be counted once, as background, with the target merely applying it. The kisse/keseh identity is also flagged as weighed in another chapter ('Pearls of Wisdom'), so its evidentiary cost must not be paid twice. The full-moon month-head element is asserted in the background without packet-internal derivation and then reused by the target's calendar section — that is the closest approach to circularity, though the eclipse synthesis proper does not require it.","strongest_rival_joint_model":"The received hubris reading joined to the packet's own stars-as-host court symbolism: the king of Babylon boasts of ascending above the heavenly court (1 Kgs 22:19; Job 38:7) to the mount of assembly in the far north (Ps 48:2, Zion), riding the theophanic cloud, to rival Elyon. This explains the mount, the north, the stars, the cloud, and the likeness claim with zero unattested morphology and no astronomical machinery.","comparative_result":"The book's joint model explains more of the discriminating details the rival leaves inert — why moed rather than a plain assembly word, why the seat shares consonants with the full-moon word, why the covering/darkness vocabulary saturates the boast, and why Dan 7:25 pairs the saints with the times — but it purchases this with two productive-but-unattested linguistic hearings and does not itself run the rival comparison. Because the chapter retains the received reading and stacks rather than displaces, the result is: the synthesis is admissible and gains modest unification weight, but its superiority over the plain reading is underdetermined on this packet.","reversal_evidence":"Reversal would follow from: an attested demonstration that keseh cannot bear a pronominal suffix or that the silence-root cannot form the consonantal eddammeh; proof that yarkete tsaphon is a frozen idiom excluding the participial hearing; a Torah-derived demonstration that months begin at conjunction/crescent (reversing the phase-inversion element); or evidence that the background symbol assignments (moon=Son's witness-throne) fail independently, which would collapse the joint model's foundation."},"category_error_audit":[{"possible_error":"Applying the vocalization admission gate to symbolic derivations, astronomical facts, or theological syntheses","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"The chapter explicitly sequences its work — 'first their permitted senses... Only after the words stand do the symbols enter' — and this audit applied the Rule 3 gate only to the five linguistic hearings, not to the symbol applications, eclipse mechanics, or Amos/Daniel syntheses."},{"possible_error":"Treating admissibility as demonstrated authorial intent","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"Phrases such as 'the words have earned their readings,' 'spoken once, heard twice,' and the composite rendered quotation present the double hearings as disclosed meaning. Rule 3 grants only possibility; Rule 1 requires underdetermined comparisons to be labeled as such. The footnotes hedge correctly, but the body prose exceeds the hedge."},{"possible_error":"Counting a lexicon's etymology or a version's rendering as proof","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"Minor instances: Strong's derivation of kisse' from a covering-root is reported as settled ('Strong's traces it to covering'), and ASV renderings are quoted as if transparent to the Hebrew. These are used as data points, not decisive proofs, so the violation of Rule 2 is marginal, but the etymology should be marked as one lexicographic proposal."},{"possible_error":"Double-counting the same evidence for the background hypothesis and the target reading","present_in_chapter":true,"explanation":"Ps 89:36-37 and the kisse/keseh identity serve both the background chapter and the target's second hearing. The chapter partially guards against this ('before any wordplay is asked to carry the identification'), but no explicit dependency map exists, and the full-moon calendar assertion flows from background to target without independent support inside the packet."},{"possible_error":"Smuggling a textual variant into a vocalization comparison","present_in_chapter":false,"explanation":"Every alternate hearing (shachar, tsafun, keseh, eddammeh) uses the identical consonants of the received text; no emendation is proposed anywhere in the chapter. The Genesis 1:16 rendering note belongs to the background packet, not the target."}],"claims_pass_as_written":["Shachar dawn/blackness wordplay as an explicitly labeled same-consonant characterization (footnoted, non-competitive)","Moed's full lexical field (appointed time/place/meeting) as legitimately in view in har moed","Tsaphon/tsafun double hearing with the north reading expressly retained (Ps 48:2)","The keseh spelling data: Prov 7:20, Ps 81:3, Job 26:9 as textual facts","Symbolic identifications applied from the frozen background (stars, mountain, moon-moedim, sun-sign)","All stated astronomical facts (eclipse only at conjunction; full moon opposite the sun; Passover phase; totality duration)","Amos 8:9-10 joined to the crucifixion darkness as prior-prophecy plus NT confirmation, with the chapter correctly refusing a natural-eclipse claim"],"claims_underdetermined":["That Isaiah intends the eddammeh 'bring the Highest to silence for myself' hearing alongside 'make myself like' (admissible via productive rules; rival better supported; intent not selectable)","That kis'i is intended to be heard as 'my full moon' (spelling facts real; suffixed keseh unattested; plain 'throne' primary)","That the eclipse-figure synthesis is the disclosed meaning of the boast rather than an admissible complementary layer (no rival joint-model audit performed)","The full-moon month-head calendar hypothesis and the consequent phase-inversion claim (asserted in background, not established within this packet)","Whether 'stars of God' refers to the righteous or the heavenly host, both being packet-supported"],"claims_fail_gate":[],"material_gaps":[{"issue":"No Rule 4 stage-4 comparison of the complete joint models: the chapter poses rhetorical questions against the plain reading but never audits the strongest rival (received hubris reading plus court/host symbolism) for what it explains and at what cost.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","why_material":"Without the comparison, the eclipse synthesis can claim only compatibility-level weight under Rule 4, leaving the chapter's central 'one act heard twice' thesis admissible but not comparatively supported.","minimal_fix_or_test":"Add one short footnote or paragraph stating what the plain reading explains, what it leaves unexplained (moed, keseh consonants, covering vocabulary, Dan 7:25's pairing), what extra assumptions each model needs, and what evidence would reverse the result."},{"issue":"Body prose asserts intended double hearings ('spoken once, heard twice'; 'the words have earned their readings') where the rubric licenses only admissibility with an underdetermined comparison.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_OVERCLAIM","why_material":"Rule 1 and Rule 3 forbid promoting an admissible hearing to demonstrated meaning; the overclaim affects the chapter's headline thesis, not a side point.","minimal_fix_or_test":"Narrow two sentences to 'admissible second hearing; the received reading stands; the comparison of intent is underdetermined,' matching the discipline already present in the footnotes."},{"issue":"The 'phase matters' calendar paragraph depends on the full-moon month-head hypothesis, which the packet asserts (background chapter) but never independently derives.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","why_material":"The inversion claim ('the two reckonings invert the lights') is only as strong as the month-head premise; on this packet it is underdetermined, and the paragraph currently reads as established.","minimal_fix_or_test":"Add a cross-reference to wherever the book independently derives the month-head phase, or conditionalize the paragraph ('if the month is headed by the full moon...')."},{"issue":"Keseh is unattested with a pronominal suffix; the 'my full moon' hearing rests on productive morphology alone, and this is not disclosed the way the Hithpael gap is.","gap_owner":"CHAPTER_MISSING_EVIDENCE","why_material":"The covered-lunar-seat hearing is the hinge between the linguistic and symbolic halves of the argument; its morphological thinness should be on the record as the eddammeh footnote's is.","minimal_fix_or_test":"One footnote sentence: 'keseh appears in Scripture only unsuffixed; the suffixed hearing rests on regular noun morphology, not an attested form.'"},{"issue":"Verification of the cited Gesenius sections, Strong's etymology of kisse', and the Job 26:9 keseh/kisseh dispute exceeds what the packet prints; this audit relied on evaluator knowledge for those confirmations.","gap_owner":"EVALUATOR_KNOWLEDGE_LIMIT","why_material":"If the Gesenius citations do not support Hithpael-with-external-object as described, the eddammeh hearing's gate pass would need re-examination.","minimal_fix_or_test":"Independent check of Gesenius §§54.2-3, 117n, 117w and a standard lexicon entry (BDB/HALOT) on keseh and Job 26:9."}],"minimal_revisions":["Narrow 'spoken once, heard twice' and 'the words have earned their readings' to admissibility language with an explicit 'comparison underdetermined' label per Rule 1.","Add a one-footnote rival joint-model audit and reversal statement (what the plain hubris reading explains, what the eclipse synthesis uniquely unifies, what would reverse it) to satisfy Rule 4 stages 4-7.","Footnote that keseh is unattested with a pronominal suffix, mirroring the candor of the existing Hithpael footnote.","Conditionalize or cross-cite the full-moon month-head premise in 'The Appointed Times Corrupted' so the phase-inversion claim visibly inherits that hypothesis's status.","Add a one-line dependency note that Ps 89:36-37 and the kisse/keseh identity are counted once, in the background, and only applied here."],"no_bloat_recommendation":"No new sections are needed. The chapter's footnote apparatus already carries the right disciplinary instincts (the shachar and hithpael footnotes are model disclosures); the five fixes above are two narrowed sentences and three footnotes totaling perhaps a dozen lines. The rival-model footnote is the only outcome-critical addition: it converts the synthesis from accommodation-weight to audited comparative weight under Rule 4 without expanding the exposition.","confidence":"MEDIUM"}
